items.title: Mississauga Council Orders Study Into Portable Washrooms for Its Busiest Parks
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga city council voted Tuesday to direct staff toward studying whether portable washrooms could be added to some of the city's busiest parks. The motion, dubbed the Porta-Potties in Parks Pilot Program, asks staff to investigate the feasibility of a seasonal portable washroom pilot at select high-use parks. Ward 4 Councillor John Kovac introduced the motion after hearing years of complaints from residents frustrated by the lack of convenient washroom access while visiting green spaces. Kovac noted that only some of the city's larger parks currently offer any bathroom facilities, since permanent structures come with a steep price tag. He argued that amenities like shelters and seating are common in Mississauga parks, but washrooms remain largely absent for that reason. In pitching the idea, Kovac pointed to Ottawa, Toronto and Hamilton as examples of cities that have already rolled out similar portable washroom programs. He called the proposal a small step for council that could bring a big relief for park visitors. Staff are now expected to report back on whether a pilot program is workable before any portable units are installed.

items.title: Road Closures Follow Fatal Hit-and-Run Involving Pickup Truck in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CBC Toronto and Insauga, a pedestrian died Tuesday evening after being hit by a pickup truck in a hit and run at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West in Mississauga. Peel Regional Police say the victim, an adult, was struck by the vehicle and pronounced dead at the scene, though officers have not released further details about who was killed. A spokesperson with Peel Regional Paramedic Services confirmed only that the victim was an adult. Police shut down all eastbound and westbound lanes on Dundas Street between Hampshire Gate and Woodchester Drive through the Winston Churchill intersection while investigators worked the scene. Drivers in the area faced significant delays, and police urged motorists to avoid the intersection while emergency crews remained on site. Peel Regional Police are asking anyone with information about the crash to call their non-emergency line at 905-453-3311.

items.title: Free Parks and Trails Line Mississauga's 22-Kilometre Lake Ontario Shoreline
items.summary: According to the St. Catharines Standard, Mississauga's stretch of Lake Ontario shoreline runs about 22 kilometres between Toronto to the east and Oakville to the west, and nearly all of it is open to the public for free. The paper notes that Mississauga tends to live in the shadow of its larger neighbour Toronto when people think of waterfront recreation, even though the two cities share the same lake and similar access to parks and trails. Rather than sandy beaches, the appeal here comes from an extensive network of parks, conservation areas and paved paths suited to picnicking, walking and cycling. The report singles out Port Credit as an essential stop, highlighting the lighthouse that sits where the Credit River meets Lake Ontario. It also points to Jack Darling Memorial Park, where visitors can often spot swans gliding along the shoreline. Every location mentioned in the roundup, from the smaller green spaces to the larger conservation areas, is described as free and open to the public. The piece frames the lakeshore as an easy escape from city life without residents needing to leave Mississauga at all.

items.title: New Poll Finds Mississauga Split Nearly Down the Middle Weeks Before Election Day
items.summary: According to a new Canada Pulse Insights survey conducted for CityNews, Mississauga residents are almost evenly split on whether their city is headed in the right direction. The poll found that 51 per cent of respondents believe Mississauga is trending positively, while 49 per cent think it is on the wrong track. Those results land just weeks ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election. CityNews describes the mayoral race as a tight three-way contest between incumbent Carolyn Parrish, Ward 2 councillor Alvin Tedjo and former mayor and ex-Ontario Liberal leader Bonnie Crombie. The near-even split on the city's direction comes as all three candidates campaign in the final weeks before voters head to the polls. No single candidate has been reported as holding a clear lead in that three-way race. The survey results were released with the municipal election just under a month away.

items.title: SIU Says No Gunfire Was Exchanged Before Toronto Officer Fatally Shot Mississauga Teen
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, the family of 19-year-old Kaleym Davy is still searching for answers more than a month after he was fatally shot by a Toronto police officer on a quiet Mississauga cul-de-sac. The province's Special Investigations Unit says the shooting happened in the early hours of Aug. 6, after five unmarked Toronto police vehicles tailed Davy's white Mercedes sedan to Delfi Road. The pursuit began hours earlier as part of a firearms investigation in downtown Toronto, according to the SIU. Davy was behind the wheel with three passengers in the car when he parked near a family member's home, and his grandmother, Marie Yee, said he was steps from his cousin's house when officers moved in. The SIU says that when officers tried to stop the vehicle shortly after midnight, Davy attempted to drive away and struck one of the officers. A collision then occurred between the Mercedes and three unmarked police vehicles, and an officer standing on the road fired through the driver's side window, fatally wounding Davy. SIU spokesperson Monica Hudon told reporters there was no evidence of an exchange of gunfire between Davy and police, though investigators recovered two firearms near the Mercedes. Yee says she still has not received an explanation for why her grandson did not make it home that night.

items.title: Council Approves Advisory Body to Track AI Data Centre Study and Report Back to Mississauga Residents
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga city council voted Tuesday to create a Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force made up of councillors, city planning staff, industry stakeholders and members of the public. The temporary body is meant to keep residents informed as senior staff carry out a comprehensive review of large data centres and any new provincial rules that could regulate the fast growing industry. Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden brought forward the motion creating the task force, which is expected to provide regular updates and what the city calls transparent reporting for the public's benefit. The move comes two weeks after council unanimously approved an interim control bylaw imposing a one to two year moratorium on new large data centre developments in Mississauga. City officials say pausing new projects will give staff more time to study the issue and any regulations the province introduces before more facilities are approved.
